newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada reviewing oil plant sale to UAE firm.
newsitem.headline: Canada reviewing oil plant sale to UAE firm.

text.p: Canadian International Trade Minister Art Eggleton said on Thursday he was reviewing a request by a firm in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) for financing to move old Canadian plants to the UAE.

Sharjah Oil Refining Co has already started implementing its C$50 million plan to ship equipment from three disused Canadian refineries and reinstall them as one plant in Sharjah, one of the seven emirates in the UAE.

The company -- partly owned by Sharjah-based FAL Oil Co, one of the biggest bunker operators at the mouth of the Mideast Gulf -- has asked the government's Export Development Corp to help finance the project, EDC spokesman Rod Giles said.
"EDC is prepared to support the Canadian portion of this package," Giles told Reuters, adding that EDC's participation would be for less than half of the C$50 million.
The majority of it would go for Canadian engineering and services in dismantling, shipping and installing the plants, he added.
He said one of the plants, from British Columbia, had already been dismantled and shipped and work had begun in Sharjah.
The other plants are in British Columbia and Nova Scotia, and the prospect of the Nova Scotia refinery being shipped off has angered many in that province, apparently prompting Eggleton's review.
The Nova Scotia plant is owned by Ultramar Canada Inc, a subsidiary of Ultramar Diamond Shamrock Corp.
"I'm reviewing the matter. The government is not directly involved," Eggleton told reporters, adding however that he did not think he could veto the deal.
He pointed out that the Ultramar plant had been closed since 1994, so no jobs were now being brought to an end.
